name: xBD / xView2: A Large-Scale Satellite Dataset for Post-Disaster Building Damage Assessment
description: xBD (the foundational dataset for the xView2 Challenge) is a large-scale, high-resolution satellite imagery dataset created to assess building damage from natural disasters. Curated by the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) and the Carnegie Mellon University Software Engineering Institute (CMU SEI), xBD contains 22,068 orthorectified satellite images (1024x1024 pixels, comprising 11,034 co-registered pre- and post-disaster image pairs) covering over 45,362 km² across 19 disaster events worldwide (earthquakes, hurricanes, tsunamis, floods, volcanic eruptions, and wildfires). It provides polygonal footprint outlines for 850,736 buildings, each graded on a four-level ordinal damage scale: no damage, minor damage, major damage, and destroyed. xBD and xView2 constitute a single unified research dataset identity.
